report.text:
EXAM: MRI LEFT KNEE WITHOUT CONTRAST

ACCESSION: 6424941491666012

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Knee pain and instability.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the left knee performed without intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:
None available.

FINDINGS:

MENISCI:
Complex horizontal tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface (series 3, image 21).

LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament demonstrates increased intrasubstance T2 signal and mild fiber irregularity compatible with mucoid degeneration/low-grade partial tearing (series 5, image 16). PCL intact.

CARTILAGE/BONE:
Focal high-grade chondral fissuring along the lateral patellar facet with mild subjacent reactive marrow edema (series 7, image 11).

Small joint effusion. No acute fracture or osteonecrosis.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Quadriceps and patellar tendons intact.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear of the posterior horn/body medial meniscus
2. Mucoid degeneration and low-grade partial tearing of the ACL
3. High-grade patellofemoral chondral fissuring involving the lateral patellar facet with mild reactive marrow edema

findings.raw_text: Focal high-grade chondral fissuring along the lateral patellar facet with mild subjacent reactive marrow edema (series 7, image 11).
findings.patientFriendlyExplanation: There is significant wear and tear of the cartilage on the outer side of your kneecap, accompanied by mild swelling in the bone underneath.

summary: The MRI shows a complex tear of the medial meniscus, a partial tear of the ACL, and significant cartilage wear on the lateral patella with underlying bone swelling. There is also a small amount of fluid in the joint, while other structures like the PCL and tendons are intact.
explanation: You have multiple injuries in your knee: a tear in the inner cartilage cushion, a mild tear in the main stabilizing ligament, and wear on the kneecap cartilage. This combination likely explains your pain and feelings of instability. You should discuss these findings with your doctor to determine if physical therapy or further treatment is needed.
